1MCQ1 mark
The unit vector perpendicular to the vectors i^−j^\hat{i}-\hat{j}i^−j^​ and i^+j^\hat{i}+\hat{j}i^+j^​ is:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea a⃗×b⃗\vec{a}\times\vec{b}a×b is perpendicular to both a⃗\vec{a}a and b⃗\vec{b}b; unit vector =a⃗×b⃗∣a⃗×b⃗∣=\dfrac{\vec{a}\times\vec{b}}{|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|}=∣a×b∣a×b​.

  1. 1

    Take the cross product of the two vectors.

    (i^−j^)×(i^+j^)=∣i^j^k^1−10110∣(\hat{i}-\hat{j})\times(\hat{i}+\hat{j}) = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \end{vmatrix}(i^−j^​)×(i^+j^​)=​i^11​j^​−11​k^00​​
  2. 2

    Expand along the first row.

    =i^(0−0)−j^(0−0)+k^(1+1)=2k^= \hat{i}(0-0)-\hat{j}(0-0)+\hat{k}(1+1) = 2\hat{k}=i^(0−0)−j^​(0−0)+k^(1+1)=2k^=i^(0−0)−j^(0−0)+k^(1+1)=2k^\displaystyle = \hat{i}(0-0)-\hat{j}(0-0)+\hat{k}(1+1) = 2\hat{k}=i^(0−0)−j^​(0−0)+k^(1+1)=2k^
  3. 3

    Divide by its magnitude 222 to get the unit vector.

    2k^2=k^\dfrac{2\hat{k}}{2} = \hat{k}22k^​=k^
    1
  4. 4

    Hence the answer is option (A).

    −k^-\hat{k}−k^ also works, but it is not an option.

Answer(A) k^\displaystyle \hat{k}k^

Watch out Picking (D): i^+j^2\dfrac{\hat{i}+\hat{j}}{\sqrt{2}}2​i^+j^​​ is one of the given directions, not perpendicular to it.

  1. 1

    Shift a⃗\vec{a}a to the other side.

    b⃗+c⃗=−a⃗\vec{b}+\vec{c} = -\vec{a}b+c=−a
  2. 2

    Square the magnitudes of both sides.

    ∣b⃗∣2+∣c⃗∣2+2 b⃗⋅c⃗=∣a⃗∣2|\vec{b}|^2+|\vec{c}|^2+2\,\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c} = |\vec{a}|^2∣b∣2+∣c∣2+2b⋅c=∣a∣2∣b⃗∣2+∣c⃗∣2+2 b⃗⋅c⃗=∣a⃗∣2\displaystyle |\vec{b}|^2+|\vec{c}|^2+2\,\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c} = |\vec{a}|^2∣b∣2+∣c∣2+2b⋅c=∣a∣2
  3. 3

    Put the given values.

    9+16+2 b⃗⋅c⃗=37b⃗⋅c⃗=6\begin{aligned} 9+16+2\,\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c} &= 37 \\ \vec{b}\cdot\vec{c} &= 6 \end{aligned}9+16+2b⋅cb⋅c​=37=6​
  4. 4

    Use b⃗⋅c⃗=∣b⃗∣∣c⃗∣cos⁡θ\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}=|\vec{b}||\vec{c}|\cos\thetab⋅c=∣b∣∣c∣cosθ.

    cos⁡θ=63×4=12  ⇒  θ=π3\cos\theta = \dfrac{6}{3\times 4} = \dfrac{1}{2} \;\Rightarrow\; \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}cosθ=3×46​=21​⇒θ=3π​cos⁡θ=63×4=12  ⇒  θ=π3\displaystyle \cos\theta = \dfrac{6}{3\times 4} = \dfrac{1}{2} \;\Rightarrow\; \theta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}cosθ=3×46​=21​⇒θ=3π​
    1
  5. 5

    Hence the answer is option (C).

Answer(C) π3\displaystyle \dfrac{\pi}{3}3π​

The value of λ\lambdaλ for which 2i^+λj^+k^2\hat{i}+\lambda\hat{j}+\hat{k}2i^+λj^​+k^ and i^−2j^+3k^\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}i^−2j^​+3k^ are perpendicular is:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Two non-zero vectors are perpendicular if and only if their dot product is 000.

  1. 1

    Perpendicular vectors have dot product zero.

    (2i^+λj^+k^)⋅(i^−2j^+3k^)=0(2\hat{i}+\lambda\hat{j}+\hat{k})\cdot(\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}) = 0(2i^+λj^​+k^)⋅(i^−2j^​+3k^)=0(2i^+λj^+k^)⋅(i^−2j^+3k^)=0\displaystyle (2\hat{i}+\lambda\hat{j}+\hat{k})\cdot(\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}) = 0(2i^+λj^​+k^)⋅(i^−2j^​+3k^)=0
  2. 2

    Multiply matching components and add.

    2(1)+λ(−2)+1(3)=0  ⇒  5−2λ=02(1)+\lambda(-2)+1(3) = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; 5-2\lambda = 02(1)+λ(−2)+1(3)=0⇒5−2λ=02(1)+λ(−2)+1(3)=0  ⇒  5−2λ=0\displaystyle 2(1)+\lambda(-2)+1(3) = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; 5-2\lambda = 02(1)+λ(−2)+1(3)=0⇒5−2λ=0
  3. 3

    Solve for λ\lambdaλ.

    λ=52\lambda = \dfrac{5}{2}λ=25​
    1
  4. 4

    Hence the answer is option (A).

Answer(A) 52\displaystyle \dfrac{5}{2}25​

Watch out Sign slip: writing +2λ+2\lambda+2λ instead of −2λ-2\lambda−2λ and getting λ=−52\lambda=-\tfrac{5}{2}λ=−25​, option (B).

If ∣a⃗∣=2|\vec{a}|=2∣a∣=2, ∣b⃗∣=5|\vec{b}|=5∣b∣=5 and a⃗⋅b⃗=8\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=8a⋅b=8, then ∣a⃗×b⃗∣|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|∣a×b∣ is:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Lagrange's identity: ∣a⃗×b⃗∣2+(a⃗⋅b⃗)2=∣a⃗∣2∣b⃗∣2|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|^2+(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b})^2=|\vec{a}|^2|\vec{b}|^2∣a×b∣2+(a⋅b)2=∣a∣2∣b∣2.

  1. 1

    Write the identity linking dot and cross products.

    ∣a⃗×b⃗∣2=∣a⃗∣2∣b⃗∣2−(a⃗⋅b⃗)2|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|^2 = |\vec{a}|^2|\vec{b}|^2-(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b})^2∣a×b∣2=∣a∣2∣b∣2−(a⋅b)2∣a⃗×b⃗∣2=∣a⃗∣2∣b⃗∣2−(a⃗⋅b⃗)2\displaystyle |\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|^2 = |\vec{a}|^2|\vec{b}|^2-(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b})^2∣a×b∣2=∣a∣2∣b∣2−(a⋅b)2

    Comes from sin⁡2θ+cos⁡2θ=1\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1sin2θ+cos2θ=1.

  2. 2

    Put the given values.

    ∣a⃗×b⃗∣2=(4)(25)−64=36|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|^2 = (4)(25)-64 = 36∣a×b∣2=(4)(25)−64=36∣a⃗×b⃗∣2=(4)(25)−64=36\displaystyle |\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|^2 = (4)(25)-64 = 36∣a×b∣2=(4)(25)−64=36
  3. 3

    Take the positive square root.

    ∣a⃗×b⃗∣=6|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}| = 6∣a×b∣=6
    1
  4. 4

    Hence the answer is option (C).

Answer(C) 6\displaystyle 66

Watch out Using ∣a⃗∣=2|\vec{a}|=2∣a∣=2 and ∣b⃗∣=5|\vec{b}|=5∣b∣=5 without squaring them, i.e. 10−6410-6410−64.

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Projection of a⃗\vec{a}a on b⃗\vec{b}b =a⃗⋅b⃗∣b⃗∣=\dfrac{\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}}{|\vec{b}|}=∣b∣a⋅b​.

  1. 1

    Find the dot product.

    a⃗⋅b⃗=2(1)+3(2)+2(1)=10\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = 2(1)+3(2)+2(1) = 10a⋅b=2(1)+3(2)+2(1)=10a⃗⋅b⃗=2(1)+3(2)+2(1)=10\displaystyle \vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = 2(1)+3(2)+2(1) = 10a⋅b=2(1)+3(2)+2(1)=10
  2. 2

    Find the magnitude of b⃗\vec{b}b, the vector projected on.

    ∣b⃗∣=1+4+1=6|\vec{b}| = \sqrt{1+4+1} = \sqrt{6}∣b∣=1+4+1​=6​
  3. 3

    Use the projection formula and rationalise.

    a⃗⋅b⃗∣b⃗∣=106=1066=563\dfrac{\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}}{|\vec{b}|} = \dfrac{10}{\sqrt{6}} = \dfrac{10\sqrt{6}}{6} = \dfrac{5\sqrt{6}}{3}∣b∣a⋅b​=6​10​=6106​​=356​​a⃗⋅b⃗∣b⃗∣=106=1066=563\displaystyle \dfrac{\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}}{|\vec{b}|} = \dfrac{10}{\sqrt{6}} = \dfrac{10\sqrt{6}}{6} = \dfrac{5\sqrt{6}}{3}∣b∣a⋅b​=6​10​=6106​​=356​​

  4. 4

    Hence the answer is option (B).

Answer(B) 563\displaystyle \dfrac{5\sqrt{6}}{3}356​​

Watch out Dividing by ∣a⃗∣=17|\vec{a}|=\sqrt{17}∣a∣=17​ instead of ∣b⃗∣|\vec{b}|∣b∣ gives option (A), the projection of b⃗\vec{b}b on a⃗\vec{a}a.

Question 4Question 6

Question 6 of 20, Level 1

6Assertion-Reason1 mark
Assertion (A): The vectors a⃗=i^+2j^+3k^\vec{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}a=i^+2j^​+3k^ and b⃗=2i^+4j^+6k^\vec{b}=2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+6\hat{k}b=2i^+4j^​+6k^ are collinear. Reason (R): Two vectors a⃗\vec{a}a and b⃗\vec{b}b are collinear if b⃗=λa⃗\vec{b}=\lambda\vec{a}b=λa for some scalar λ\lambdaλ.

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea a⃗\vec{a}a and b⃗\vec{b}b are collinear   ⟺  b⃗=λa⃗\iff \vec{b}=\lambda\vec{a}⟺b=λa for some scalar λ\lambdaλ.

  1. 1

    Check Assertion: compare b⃗\vec{b}b with a⃗\vec{a}a.

    b⃗=2i^+4j^+6k^=2(i^+2j^+3k^)=2a⃗\vec{b} = 2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+6\hat{k} = 2(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}) = 2\vec{a}b=2i^+4j^​+6k^=2(i^+2j^​+3k^)=2ab⃗=2i^+4j^+6k^=2(i^+2j^+3k^)=2a⃗\displaystyle \vec{b} = 2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+6\hat{k} = 2(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}) = 2\vec{a}b=2i^+4j^​+6k^=2(i^+2j^​+3k^)=2a
  2. 2

    So b⃗=2a⃗\vec{b}=2\vec{a}b=2a; the vectors are collinear. A is true.

  3. 3

    Reason is the standard condition for collinear vectors. R is true.

  4. 4

    A follows directly from R with λ=2\lambda=2λ=2. R explains A.

  5. 5

    Hence the correct option is (A).

    1
Answer(A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

Watch out Choosing (B) because R is a general rule; a general rule that is used to prove A does explain A.

    Write the formula for the area.

    Area=∣a⃗×b⃗∣\text{Area} = |\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|Area=∣a×b∣
    ½
  2. 2

    Set up the cross product as a determinant.

    a⃗×b⃗=∣i^j^k^11−11−11∣\vec{a}\times\vec{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 \end{vmatrix}a×b=​i^11​j^​1−1​k^−11​​

    Expand along the first row.

    =i^(1−1)−j^(1+1)+k^(−1−1)=−2j^−2k^\begin{aligned} &= \hat{i}(1-1)-\hat{j}(1+1)+\hat{k}(-1-1) \\ &= -2\hat{j}-2\hat{k} \end{aligned}​=i^(1−1)−j^​(1+1)+k^(−1−1)=−2j^​−2k^​

  4. 4

    Find its magnitude.

    ∣a⃗×b⃗∣=0+4+4=8=22|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}| = \sqrt{0+4+4} = \sqrt{8} = 2\sqrt{2}∣a×b∣=0+4+4​=8​=22​∣a⃗×b⃗∣=0+4+4=8=22\displaystyle |\vec{a}\times\vec{b}| = \sqrt{0+4+4} = \sqrt{8} = 2\sqrt{2}∣a×b∣=0+4+4​=8​=22​
    ½

    State the area with units.

    Area=22 sq units\text{Area} = 2\sqrt{2}\ \text{sq units}Area=22​ sq unitsArea=22 sq units\displaystyle \text{Area} = 2\sqrt{2}\ \text{sq units}Area=22​ sq units
    ½
AnswerArea =22\displaystyle =2\sqrt{2}=22​ sq units

Find a unit vector perpendicular to both a⃗=i^+j^+k^\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}a=i^+j^​+k^ and b⃗=i^+2j^+3k^\vec{b}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}b=i^+2j^​+3k^.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Unit vector perpendicular to a⃗\vec{a}a and b⃗\vec{b}b =±a⃗×b⃗∣a⃗×b⃗∣=\pm\dfrac{\vec{a}\times\vec{b}}{|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|}=±∣a×b∣a×b​.

  1. 1

    Set up a⃗×b⃗\vec{a}\times\vec{b}a×b as a determinant.

    a⃗×b⃗=∣i^j^k^111123∣\vec{a}\times\vec{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \end{vmatrix}a×b=​i^11​j^​12​k^13​​
    ½
  2. 2

    Expand along the first row.

    =i^(3−2)−j^(3−1)+k^(2−1)=i^−2j^+k^= \hat{i}(3-2)-\hat{j}(3-1)+\hat{k}(2-1) = \hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k}=i^(3−2)−j^​(3−1)+k^(2−1)=i^−2j^​+k^=i^(3−2)−j^(3−1)+k^(2−1)=i^−2j^+k^\displaystyle = \hat{i}(3-2)-\hat{j}(3-1)+\hat{k}(2-1) = \hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k}=i^(3−2)−j^​(3−1)+k^(2−1)=i^−2j^​+k^
    ½
  3. 3

    Find its magnitude.

    ∣a⃗×b⃗∣=1+4+1=6|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}| = \sqrt{1+4+1} = \sqrt{6}∣a×b∣=1+4+1​=6​∣a⃗×b⃗∣=1+4+1=6\displaystyle |\vec{a}\times\vec{b}| = \sqrt{1+4+1} = \sqrt{6}∣a×b∣=1+4+1​=6​
    ½

  2. 2

    b⃗×c⃗\vec{b}\times\vec{c}b×c is also perpendicular to both, so a⃗\vec{a}a is parallel to it.

    1=∣λ∣×1×1×121 = |\lambda|\times 1\times 1\times\dfrac{1}{2}1=∣λ∣×1×1×21​1=∣λ∣×1×1×12\displaystyle 1 = |\lambda|\times 1\times 1\times\dfrac{1}{2}1=∣λ∣×1×1×21​

Let a⃗=i^+4j^+2k^\vec{a}=\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+2\hat{k}a=i^+4j^​+2k^, b⃗=3i^−2j^+7k^\vec{b}=3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+7\hat{k}b=3i^−2j^​+7k^ and c⃗=2i^−j^+4k^\vec{c}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+4\hat{k}c=2i^−j^​+4k^. Find a vector d⃗\vec{d}d which is perpendicular to both a⃗\vec{a}a and b⃗\vec{b}b, and c⃗⋅d⃗=15\vec{c}\cdot\vec{d}=15c⋅d=15.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Any vector perpendicular to both a⃗\vec{a}a and b⃗\vec{b}b is λ(a⃗×b⃗)\lambda(\vec{a}\times\vec{b})λ(a×b).

  1. 1

    d⃗\vec{d}d is perpendicular to both a⃗\vec{a}a and b⃗\vec{b}b, so it is parallel to a⃗×b⃗\vec{a}\times\vec{b}a×b.

    d⃗=λ(a⃗×b⃗) for some scalar λ\vec{d} = \lambda(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}) \text{ for some scalar } \lambdad=λ(a×b) for some scalar λd⃗=λ(a⃗×b⃗) for some scalar λ\displaystyle \vec{d} = \lambda(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}) \text{ for some scalar } \lambdad=λ(a×b) for some scalar λ
    1
  2. 2

    Set up a⃗×b⃗\vec{a}\times\vec{b}a×b as a determinant.

    a⃗×b⃗=∣i^j^k^1423−27∣\vec{a}\times\vec{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 4 & 2 \\ 3 & -2 & 7 \end{vmatrix}a×b=​i^13​j^​4−2​k^27​​
    ½
  3. 3

    Expand along the first row.

    =i^(28+4)−j^(7−6)+k^(−2−12)= \hat{i}(28+4)-\hat{j}(7-6)+\hat{k}(-2-12)=i^(28+4)−j^​(7−6)+k^(−2−12)=i^(28+4)−j^(7−6)+k^(−2−12)\displaystyle = \hat{i}(28+4)-\hat{j}(7-6)+\hat{k}(-2-12)=i^(28+4)−j^​(7−6)+k^(−2−12)
    ½
  4. 4

    Simplify.

    a⃗×b⃗=32i^−j^−14k^\vec{a}\times\vec{b} = 32\hat{i}-\hat{j}-14\hat{k}a×b=32i^−j^​−14k^a⃗×b⃗=32i^−j^−14k^\displaystyle \vec{a}\times\vec{b} = 32\hat{i}-\hat{j}-14\hat{k}a×b=32i^−j^​−14k^
    ½
  5. 5

    So d⃗\vec{d}d is:

    d⃗=λ(32i^−j^−14k^)=32λi^−λj^−14λk^\vec{d} = \lambda(32\hat{i}-\hat{j}-14\hat{k}) = 32\lambda\hat{i}-\lambda\hat{j}-14\lambda\hat{k}d=λ(32i^−j^​−14k^)=32λi^−λj^​−14λk^d⃗=λ(32i^−j^−14k^)=32λi^−λj^−14λk^\displaystyle \vec{d} = \lambda(32\hat{i}-\hat{j}-14\hat{k}) = 32\lambda\hat{i}-\lambda\hat{j}-14\lambda\hat{k}d=λ(32i^−j^​−14k^)=32λi^−λj^​−14λk^
    ½
  6. 6

    Use the condition c⃗⋅d⃗=15\vec{c}\cdot\vec{d}=15c⋅d=15.

    (2i^−j^+4k^)⋅(32λi^−λj^−14λk^)=1564λ+λ−56λ=15\begin{aligned} (2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+4\hat{k})\cdot(32\lambda\hat{i}-\lambda\hat{j}-14\lambda\hat{k}) &= 15 \\ 64\lambda+\lambda-56\lambda &= 15 \end{aligned}(2i^−j^​+4k^)⋅(32λi^−λj^​−14λk^)64λ+λ−56λ​=15=15​
    1
  7. 7

    Solve for λ\lambdaλ.

    9λ=15  ⇒  λ=539\lambda = 15 \;\Rightarrow\; \lambda = \dfrac{5}{3}9λ=15⇒λ=35​9λ=15  ⇒  λ=53\displaystyle 9\lambda = 15 \;\Rightarrow\; \lambda = \dfrac{5}{3}9λ=15⇒λ=35​
    ½
  8. 8

    Substitute λ\lambdaλ to get d⃗\vec{d}d.

    d⃗=53(32i^−j^−14k^)=13(160i^−5j^−70k^)\vec{d} = \dfrac{5}{3}(32\hat{i}-\hat{j}-14\hat{k}) = \dfrac{1}{3}(160\hat{i}-5\hat{j}-70\hat{k})d=35​(32i^−j^​−14k^)=31​(160i^−5j^​−70k^)d⃗=53(32i^−j^−14k^)=13(160i^−5j^−70k^)\displaystyle \vec{d} = \dfrac{5}{3}(32\hat{i}-\hat{j}-14\hat{k}) = \dfrac{1}{3}(160\hat{i}-5\hat{j}-70\hat{k})d=35​(32i^−j^​−14k^)=31​(160i^−5j^​−70k^)
    ½
Answerd⃗=13(160i^−5j^−70k^)\displaystyle \vec{d}=\dfrac{1}{3}(160\hat{i}-5\hat{j}-70\hat{k})d=31​(160i^−5j^​−70k^)

Watch out Stopping at d⃗=λ(a⃗×b⃗)\vec{d}=\lambda(\vec{a}\times\vec{b})d=λ(a×b); the condition c⃗⋅d⃗=15\vec{c}\cdot\vec{d}=15c⋅d=15 fixes λ\lambdaλ, so d⃗\vec{d}d is unique (no ±\pm±).

  1. 1

    Find a⃗+b⃗\vec{a}+\vec{b}a+b.

    Set up their cross product.

    (a⃗+b⃗)×(a⃗−b⃗)=∣i^j^k^2340−1−2∣(\vec{a}+\vec{b})\times(\vec{a}-\vec{b}) = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & -2 \end{vmatrix}(a+b)×(a−b)=​i^20​j^​3−1​k^4−2​​
  4. 4

    Expand along the first row.

    =i^(−6+4)−j^(−4−0)+k^(−2−0)=−2i^+4j^−2k^\begin{aligned} &= \hat{i}(-6+4)-\hat{j}(-4-0)+\hat{k}(-2-0) \\ &= -2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-2\hat{k} \end{aligned}​=i^(−6+4)−j^​(−4−0)+k^(−2−0)=−2i^+4j^​−2k^​
    1
  5. 5

    Find its magnitude.

    4+16+4=24=26\sqrt{4+16+4} = \sqrt{24} = 2\sqrt{6}4+16+4​=24​=26​
    ½
  6. 6

    Multiply the unit vector by 555; take both directions.

    ±5⋅−2i^+4j^−2k^26=±56(−i^+2j^−k^)\pm 5\cdot\dfrac{-2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-2\hat{k}}{2\sqrt{6}} = \pm\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{6}}(-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k})±5⋅26​−2i^+4j^​−2k^​=±6​5​(−i^+2j^​−k^)±5⋅−2i^+4j^−2k^26=±56(−i^+2j^−k^)\displaystyle \pm 5\cdot\dfrac{-2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-2\hat{k}}{2\sqrt{6}} = \pm\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{6}}(-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k})±5⋅26​−2i^+4j^​−2k^​=±6​5​(−i^+2j^​−k^)
    ½
Answer±56(−i^+2j^−k^)\displaystyle \pm\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{6}}(-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k})±6​5​(−i^+2j^​−k^), i.e. ±566(−i^+2j^−k^)\displaystyle \pm\dfrac{5\sqrt{6}}{6}(-\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k})±656​​(−i^+2j^​−k^)

Case Study: A toy drone starts from the origin OOO. It first moves to point AAA with OA→=2i^+3j^+k^\overrightarrow{OA}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+\hat{k}OA=2i^+3j^​+k^ and is then commanded to point BBB with OB→=4i^+j^+3k^\overrightarrow{OB}=4\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}OB=4i^+j^​+3k^ (units in metres).
  1. (i)Find the displacement vector AB→\overrightarrow{AB}AB.1 mark
  2. (ii)Find the distance travelled from AAA to BBB and the unit vector along AB→\overrightarrow{AB}AB.1 mark
  3. (iii)Find the angle between OA→\overrightarrow{OA}OA and OB→\overrightarrow{OB}OB.2 marks

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea AB→=OB→−OA→\overrightarrow{AB}=\overrightarrow{OB}-\overrightarrow{OA}AB=OB−OA; cos⁡θ=OA→⋅OB→∣OA→∣∣OB→∣\cos\theta=\dfrac{\overrightarrow{OA}\cdot\overrightarrow{OB}}{|\overrightarrow{OA}||\overrightarrow{OB}|}cosθ=∣OA∣∣OB∣OA⋅OB​.

(i)1 mark

  1. 1

    Displacement = final position vector −-− initial position vector.

    AB→=OB→−OA→\overrightarrow{AB} = \overrightarrow{OB}-\overrightarrow{OA}AB=OB−OAAB→=OB→−OA→\displaystyle \overrightarrow{AB} = \overrightarrow{OB}-\overrightarrow{OA}AB=OB−OA
    ½
  2. 2

    Subtract component-wise.

    AB→=(4−2)i^+(1−3)j^+(3−1)k^=2i^−2j^+2k^\overrightarrow{AB} = (4-2)\hat{i}+(1-3)\hat{j}+(3-1)\hat{k} = 2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}AB=(4−2)i^+(1−3)j^​+(3−1)k^=2i^−2j^​+2k^AB→=(4−2)i^+(1−3)j^+(3−1)k^=2i^−2j^+2k^\displaystyle \overrightarrow{AB} = (4-2)\hat{i}+(1-3)\hat{j}+(3-1)\hat{k} = 2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}AB=(4−2)i^+(1−3)j^​+(3−1)k^=2i^−2j^​+2k^
    ½
Answer (i)AB→=2i^−2j^+2k^\displaystyle \overrightarrow{AB}=2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}AB=2i^−2j^​+2k^

(ii)1 mark

  1. 1

    Distance ABABAB is the magnitude of AB→\overrightarrow{AB}AB.

    ∣AB→∣=4+4+4=12=23 m|\overrightarrow{AB}| = \sqrt{4+4+4} = \sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3}\ \text{m}∣AB∣=4+4+4​=12​=23​ m∣AB→∣=4+4+4=12=23 m\displaystyle |\overrightarrow{AB}| = \sqrt{4+4+4} = \sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3}\ \text{m}∣AB∣=4+4+4​=12​=23​ m
